claim.quote: CDMS data give limits on the spin-independent WIMP-nucleon elastic-scattering cross-section that exclude unexplored parameter space above 10 GeV c^{-2} WIMP mass and, at > 84% CL, the entire 3$\sigma$ allowed region for the WIMP signal reported by the DAMA experiment.

name: Exclusion Limits on the WIMP-Nucleon Cross-Section from the Cryogenic Dark Matter Search

summary.plain: CDMS I looked for dark matter particles with germanium and silicon crystals and saw none it could attribute to them, ruling out at more than 84% confidence the whole region where DAMA had reported a signal.
summary.technical: 96 live days with three 165 g Ge BLIP detectors (10.6 kg d final exposure after cuts) plus a 33-live-day 100 g Si ZIP run, at 17 m.w.e. beneath Stanford; the Si nuclear recoils are used to measure the unvetoed neutron background.

title: Exclusion Limits on the WIMP-Nucleon Cross-Section from the Cryogenic Dark Matter Search
why_it_matters: First direct test of the DAMA claim with a different target and event-by-event background rejection.
